summary: Count to 20 by ones.
Count backward from 10 by ones.
Say which number comes just after or just before a number, counting to 10.
Recognize the written numbers 0 to 10.
Count up to 10 objects one by one, and know the last number said is how many.
See that each next number when counting means one more.
Show a number up to 10 with objects, pictures or a written number, and say how many.
See how many at a glance: up to 3 in any arrangement, up to 5 in familiar patterns like dice.
Compare two groups up to 10: more than, equal to or less than, by matching and counting.
Break numbers up to 5 into parts in more than one way.
Act out, draw or explain adding and taking away within 5, without written symbols.
Find how many more make 5, with objects, fingers or drawings.
Spot and continue repeating patterns (ABAB, AABB, ABCABC) with objects, shapes or sounds.
Describe things that can be measured, like length, height and weight: long, heavy, wide.
Compare two objects directly: longer or shorter, heavier or lighter, taller or shorter.
Sort circles, triangles and rectangles (squares too), and tell shapes that belong from ones that don't.
Match and name circles, triangles and rectangles whatever their size or which way they face.
Match and sort cubes, spheres and cylinders.
Sort objects into groups.
Compare the groups: which has more, less or the same (up to 10 in a group).
Count to 100 by ones and by tens.
Count forward from any number within 100, not just 1.
Count backward from any number up to 20.
Write the numbers 0 to 20.
Write a numeral to show how many objects there are, up to 20 (0 means none).
Count up to 20 objects one at a time, and know the last number says how many.
See that each next number when counting means one more.
Tell how many are in a small group at a glance, without counting.
Build and break apart 11–19 as one ten and some more ones.
Compare two amounts up to 20 as greater, less or equal, using objects or numerals.
Break numbers up to 10 into pairs in more than one way, and record each one.
Show adding and taking away within 10 with objects, fingers, drawings or acting it out.
Solve adding and taking-away story problems within 10.
Spot, continue and make repeating patterns, like AABAAB or ABCABC.
Describe what can be measured: long or short, heavy or light, full or empty.
Compare two objects: which is taller, shorter, heavier or lighter.
Put up to 3 objects in order by size, like tallest to shortest.
Describe where things are: above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to.
Name flat and solid shapes whatever their size or which way they face.
Tell flat shapes from solid shapes.
Compare flat and solid shapes by their sides, corners and faces.
Draw flat shapes and build models of solid shapes.
Put small shapes together to make bigger ones.
Sort objects into groups and count each group, up to 20.
Put sorted groups in order from most to fewest.
Count forward and backward within 120 from any number, and by tens.
Read and write numbers to 120, and use a numeral to show how many.
Understand two-digit numbers as tens and ones, and split them in different ways.
Show whole numbers as distances from 0 on a number line.
Compare two-digit numbers using tens, ones or a number line, with >, = and <.
Estimate where a number sits on a number line using 10, 50 and 100 as guides.
Use turn-around facts and grouping to make adding easier.
Subtract by thinking of the matching addition fact.
Add and subtract within 20 quickly, using counting on, making ten and doubles.
Add within 100 using models and place value, making a new ten when needed.
Find 10 more or 10 less than a two-digit number in your head.
Subtract multiples of 10 within 90.
Subtract a one-digit number from a two-digit number without regrouping.
Split circles and rectangles into halves and fourths; more shares means smaller ones.
Understand the equal sign and decide whether equations are true or false.
Solve adding and subtracting story problems within 20, with the unknown anywhere.
Find the missing number in an addition or subtraction equation.
Put three objects in order by length, and compare two lengths using a third.
Measure length by lining up same-size units end to end.
Tell which features make a shape what it is, and which ones don't matter.
Put flat or solid shapes together to make new shapes.
Tell time to the hour, half hour and quarter hour, and estimate how long things take.
Name coins and bills and know what each is worth.
Ask a question, collect answers, and show them in tally charts and picture graphs.
Understand three-digit numbers as hundreds, tens and ones, and split them different ways.
Count within 1000 from any number, and skip-count by 2s, 5s, 10s and 100s.
Read and write numbers to 1000 as numerals, words and expanded form.
Compare three-digit numbers by place value or a number line, using >, = and <.
Estimate numbers on a number line and check whether sums and differences make sense.
Add and subtract within 20 quickly, using strategies like doubles plus one.
Show sums and differences within 100 as jumps on a number line.
Add and subtract within 100 fluently, picking the best strategy.
Add and subtract within 1000 using models and place value.
Add or subtract 10 or 100 in your head, for numbers 100–900.
Split shapes into halves, thirds and fourths; equal shares can differ in shape.
Solve one-step adding and subtracting story problems within 100.
Solve two-step adding and subtracting story problems within 100.
Tell whether a group of up to 20 is odd or even, and write an even number as a double.
Measure length with a ruler, yardstick, meter stick or tape.
Measure something twice with different units and compare the numbers.
Estimate lengths in inches, feet, centimeters and meters.
Measure how much longer one object is than another.
Recognize and draw shapes by their angles and faces.
Find and draw lines of symmetry that fold a shape into matching halves.
Tell and write time to the nearest minute on digital and analog clocks.
Estimate and work out elapsed time to the hour and half hour.
Solve money problems up to $20 with bills and coins, using $ and ¢.
Ask a question, collect data, and show it in picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots.
Read, write, round and compare whole numbers within 10,000.
Understand multiplying as equal groups: 5 × 7 is 5 groups of 7.
Understand dividing as sharing equally or making equal groups.
Use turn-around facts, grouping and breaking apart to make multiplying easier.
Solve division by finding a missing factor: 32 ÷ 8 asks 8 × ? = 32.
Estimate sums and differences within 1,000, and know when an estimate is enough.
Add and subtract within 1,000 fluently, picking the best strategy.
Multiply one-digit numbers by multiples of 10, like 9 × 80.
Multiply and divide within 100, and know the times tables from memory.
Understand a fraction as equal parts of a whole: 3/4 is three parts of size 1/4.
Name a fraction of a set: 2 red balls out of 5 balls is 2/5 of the set.
Place fractions on a number line.
Find equivalent fractions and compare fractions by thinking about their size.
Solve multiplying and dividing story problems within 100 about groups, arrays and area.
Solve two-step story problems with all four operations, and check the answer makes sense.
Find number patterns and explain them, like why 4 times any number is even.
Measure lengths to the nearest half or quarter unit with a ruler.
Solve story problems adding and subtracting minutes, using a number line.
Measure and estimate liquid volume and mass in liters, grams and kilograms.
Solve one-step story problems about mass or liquid volume in the same units.
See that shapes in different groups can share features, like quadrilaterals.
Understand area and measure it by counting unit squares.
Connect area to multiplying and adding, including shapes made of rectangles.
Understand perimeter as the distance around a shape, and measure it.
Solve perimeter problems, including finding a missing side.
Make scaled picture graphs, bar graphs and line plots, and tell the story in the data.
Read, write, round and compare whole numbers up to 1,000,000.
Understand that each place is worth ten times the place to its right.
Add and subtract within 1,000,000 fluently, including with the standard method.
Multiply multi-digit numbers by multiples of 10, like 34 × 20, using place value.
Multiply up to four digits by one digit, and two digits by two digits.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by one-digit numbers, with remainders.
Keep practicing times tables and division facts within 100 until they're quick.
Find factor pairs and multiples, and tell prime from composite numbers.
Make equivalent fractions and explain why they are equal, using models.
Compare fractions with different numerators and denominators.
Break a fraction into a sum of smaller fractions, like 3/8 = 1/8 + 2/8.
Add and subtract fractions with like denominators, including story problems.
Multiply a fraction by a whole number.
Add fractions with denominators of 10 and 100.
Write tenths and hundredths as decimals.
Compare decimals to hundredths using >, = and <.
Read multiplying as comparing: 35 is 5 times as many as 7.
Solve story problems that compare by multiplying or dividing.
Tell comparing by multiplying (3 times as many) from comparing by adding (3 more).
Solve multi-step story problems, including ones with remainders.
Convert measurements from a larger unit to a smaller one, like feet to inches.
Solve story problems about distance, time, volume, mass and money.
Use area and perimeter formulas for rectangles, including finding a missing side.
Find the area of a triangle by relating it to a rectangle.
Understand angles and measuring them in degrees.
Measure angles with a protractor, and estimate and sketch angles.
Find missing angles by adding and subtracting.
Draw points, lines, rays, angles, and parallel and perpendicular lines.
Sort shapes by parallel or perpendicular sides and angles, and spot right triangles.
Make and read bar graphs and line plots, and see how a graph's design changes its message.
Understand that each place is ten times the place to its right and a tenth of the one to its left.
Explain patterns when multiplying or dividing by powers of 10, and use exponents.
Read, write, round and compare decimals to thousandths.
Multiply multi-digit whole numbers fluently, including with the standard method.
Divide up to four-digit numbers by two-digit divisors.
Add and subtract decimals to hundredths.
Multiply and divide decimals to hundredths in story problems.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators.
Solve fraction story problems, including ones with unlike denominators.
Understand a fraction as a division: 3/4 is 3 ÷ 4.
Find a fraction of a whole number, like 3/4 × 2.
Multiply a fraction by a fraction, including finding areas with fraction side lengths.
Multiply fractions when one or both are greater than 1, like 3/2 × 5/4.
Understand multiplying as scaling something up or down.
Solve real-world problems multiplying fractions and mixed numbers.
Divide unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions.
Evaluate expressions with parentheses, brackets and braces.
Write and read simple expressions without working them out.
Make number patterns from rules, compare them, and show them in tables and graphs.
Convert between units in the same measurement system to solve multi-step problems.
See that features of a shape family belong to every shape in it.
Sort triangles and quadrilaterals into families by their sides and angles.
Understand volume and measure it by counting unit cubes.
Find volumes of rectangular prisms with formulas, including solids built from prisms.
Understand the coordinate plane, and plot and name points with ordered pairs.
Plot points in the first quadrant to solve problems.
Make and read graphs, find the mode and range, and judge whether a graph is misleading.
